config: selected: r=0.375, lambda=1.0, n_cal=16384, seed 0, M=20

step1_ffn_output.note: the ridge is a PARTIAL correction: it removes ~21% of the perturbation-induced FFN-output change on held-out data, not ~100%

step2_residual_stream.note: the FFN contributes <half the residual-stream norm, so a 17.6% FFN change is only a 7.0% block-output change

step3_score_composition.note: member disagreement is <1% of the predictive entropy, so the OOD score is dominated by the base model's own confidence

step4_ranking.note: AUROC is a pure ranking statistic; rankings this correlated cannot produce different AUROC

interpretation: The correction does what it claims -- it removes the reducible part of the perturbation (MI drops 29%, median logit MSE 2.3x) -- but at r=0.375 the disagreement term it acts on is <1% of the score, so improving it cannot move AUROC. The r-sweep confirms the mechanism: the corrected-vs-uncorrected AUROC gap grows monotonically (+0.12 at r=0.25, +0.25 at 0.375, +0.39 at 0.5, +1.39 at 1.0, +4.57 at 2.0) as the disagreement term grows.
